chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who commits a major sin from the major sins and then dies. Does that exit him from Islam? And if he is punished, is his punishment like the punishment of the polytheists, or does he have a period and an end? He said: 'The one who commits a major sin from the major sins and alleges that it is permissible, that exits him from Islam and he is punished with the severest punishment. And if he was acknowledging that he sinned and died upon it, that exits him from faith (Iman) and does not exit him from Islam, and his punishment is lighter than the punishment of the first one.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a major sinner who is removed from Islam versus one who is only removed from faith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'intermediate status' (manzila bayn al-manzilatayn) by distinguishing between major sins committed with conviction of permissibility versus those committed with acknowledgment of fault. It establishes that while such a sinner remains within the fold of Islam, their faith is diminished, leading to a punishment distinct from that of polytheists. This distinction underscores the Shia view that major sins do not necessarily equate to apostasy unless accompanied by a denial of their prohibition.
